gmail.s1: Open Gmail's Forwarding and POP/IMAP settings, signed in as this address.
gmail.s2: Choose Add a forwarding address and paste the address above.
gmail.s3: Gmail sends a confirmation email. It arrives in opendesk as a ticket: open it and click the link, or copy the code into Gmail.
gmail.s4: Back in Gmail, select Forward a copy of incoming mail to the new address and save.

workspace.s1: For one mailbox, follow the Gmail steps while signed in as that user.
workspace.s2: For a group or many users, an admin opens Routing in the Google Admin console (Apps, Google Workspace, Gmail).
workspace.s3: Add a routing rule for Inbound mail to the address, choose Modify message, then Add more recipients, and add the address above.
workspace.s4: Save. Changes can take a few minutes to apply.

microsoft.s1: An admin opens the Anti-spam policies in Microsoft Defender, edits the Outbound policy and sets Automatic forwarding rules to On.
microsoft.s2: In the Exchange admin center, open Mailboxes and select the mailbox.
microsoft.s3: Under Mail flow settings, edit Email forwarding: turn it on, paste the address above and keep a copy in the mailbox.
microsoft.s4: No access to the admin center? After step 1, open Forwarding in Outlook's settings as the mailbox, turn it on, paste the address above and keep a copy.

outlook.s1: Open Outlook.com's Forwarding settings, signed in as this address.
outlook.s2: Turn on Enable forwarding and paste the address above.
outlook.s3: Turn on Keep a copy of forwarded messages and save.

other.s1: In your email provider's settings, find forwarding. Some call it a redirect or an alias.
other.s2: Forward all mail for this address to the address above, keeping a copy if you want one.

gmail.banner: An app password connects Gmail or Google Workspace over IMAP and SMTP in about two minutes.
gmail.s1Sub: Google only offers app passwords on accounts that have it on.
gmail.s1a: Open your Google Account's security page and find 2-Step Verification under How you sign in to Google.
gmail.s1b: Turn it on with a phone prompt, an authenticator app or a text message.
gmail.s1Note: On Google Workspace an admin can require or block 2-Step Verification for the organization. Accounts in Advanced Protection can't have app passwords.
gmail.s2Sub: A 16-letter password Google makes for one app. opendesk stores it encrypted.
gmail.s2a: Open the app passwords page. Google may ask you to sign in again.
gmail.s2b: Type opendesk as the app name and choose Create.
gmail.s2c: Copy the 16 letters it shows. The spaces don't matter.
gmail.s2Note: No app passwords page? 2-Step Verification is still off, or your Google Workspace admin has turned app passwords off for your organization. Ask them to allow app passwords for your account.
gmail.s3Sub: Paste the app password. Nothing else to type.
gmail.lengthHint: Google app passwords are 16 letters. This looks like something else, maybe the account password. It's checked when you connect either way.
gmail.s3Note: Use the address you sign in to Google with, not an alias. Deleting the app password in your Google Account disconnects the mailbox.

fastmail.s3: Copy the password and paste it below.

slack.description: Mirror email tickets into Slack threads and work them by talking to Ollie.
slack.setup: Create a Slack app with the chat:write, app_mentions:read, channels:read, groups:read, channels:history, groups:history and files:read bot scopes, install it, then paste its bot token and signing secret. After connecting, opendesk shows the setup steps to finish in Slack.
steps: In your Slack app, open Event Subscriptions, turn it on and paste the address above as the Request URL.
Under Subscribe to bot events, add app_mention, message.channels and message.groups, then save.
Open Interactivity & Shortcuts, turn it on and use the same address as its Request URL.
Open Slash Commands, create /opendesk and use the same address as its Request URL.
Invite the bot to each channel you route tickets to: /invite @your-bot.
slack.noChannels: The bot isn't in any channel yet. Invite it with /invite @your-bot in Slack, then refresh.

discord.description: Mirror email tickets into Discord threads and work them by talking to Ollie.
discord.setup: Create a Discord bot, turn on its Message Content intent and copy its token and public key. opendesk finds its servers and registers the interactions endpoint and commands.
discord.noChannels: No text channels found. Give the bot access to a text channel in this server, then refresh.

telegram.description: Mirror email tickets into Telegram forum topics and work them by talking to Ollie.
telegram.setup: Create a bot with BotFather, turn off its privacy mode (/setprivacy) and paste its token. opendesk sets up the webhook. Then make the bot an admin of a forum group.
telegram.noChannels: No forum groups yet. Make the bot an admin of a group with topics turned on, or send a message in a group it's already in, then refresh.

google_chat.description: Mirror email tickets into Google Chat spaces and work them by talking to Ollie.
google_chat.setup: Enable the Google Chat API and create a service account key with the chat.bot scope. Configure a standard Chat app, not a Google Workspace add-on, for the same project and add it to the spaces you want to use.
steps: In Google Cloud Console, enable the Google Chat API and configure a standard Chat app, not a Google Workspace add-on, for the project used by this service account.
Set the connection URL and authentication audience to the webhook address above. Choose HTTP endpoint URL as the authentication audience.
Add an /opendesk slash command and subscribe the app to message, message update, message delete, card click, app added and app removed events.
Add the Chat app to each space you want to route tickets to, then refresh the space list.
google_chat.noChannels: No spaces are available. Add the Chat app to a named space, then refresh.
